content:
{'translation': 'After more than a decade without introducing touchscreens to its Mac laptop lineup, Apple is finally set to launch its first MacBook with a touchscreen as early as October. The new product will debut alongside the next-generation redesigned MacBook Pro, which may be called the MacBook Ultra.', 'index': 0}

{'translation': 'Of course, rumours are still rumours — but virtually every credible source agrees that the MacBook Pro will gain touch support later this year. Apple has even dropped several hints in macOS 27: touch support for Sidecar, pull-to-refresh functionality, and slightly enlarged menu bar items.', 'index': 1}

{'translation': 'As a 13-inch MacBook Air user, the last change is particularly annoying, because content that previously fit within the left side of the "notch" now starts to overflow beyond it.', 'index': 2}

{'translation': "You could say it's all coincidental, but the reality is likely exactly what it appears to be. Either way, here are the selling points the first touchscreen MacBook will bring.", 'index': 3}

{'translation': 'OLED, Dynamic Island', 'index': 4}

{'translation': 'On the display front, the redesigned MacBook Pro will feature a Tandem OLED display similar to the technology used in the iPad Pro, which is often hailed as one of the best mobile device screens on the market. Tandem OLED consists of stacked OLED panels, delivering superior colours, higher contrast, and greater brightness.', 'index': 5}

{'translation': 'Other reports suggest the new product will feature a Dynamic Island, but slightly smaller than the one on iPhone, though it will not support Face ID.', 'index': 6}

{'translation': 'Software optimisations', 'index': 7}

{'translation': "According to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, Apple will make several special optimisations for the first touchscreen MacBook Pro, beyond what's already visible in the macOS 27 beta:", 'index': 8}

{'translation': '"For example, when users touch buttons or controls, a new type of menu will pop up around their fingers, offering more touch-related options. The software will also display the most appropriate set of controls based on the user\'s previous interaction habits. Additionally, if users tap a menu bar item at the top of the screen, that set of controls will be enlarged for easier selection with fingers."', 'index': 9}

{'translation': 'M5 Pro and M5 Max chips', 'index': 10}

{'translation': "Although earlier reports suggested the redesigned MacBook Pro would debut M6 Pro and M6 Max chips, Apple has now skipped that batch of chips to accelerate M7 development. This means the first 2nm chips won't be used in the redesigned MacBook Pro, which will stick with the current M5 Pro and M5 Max chips.", 'index': 11}

{'translation': "However, a base model version won't be available for now; though there are rumours that Apple will release a redesigned MacBook Pro base model with the M7 chip as early as next spring.", 'index': 12}

{'translation': 'Slightly thinner chassis', 'index': 13}

{'translation': "One design rumour about the new MacBook Pro is that it will be slightly thinner and lighter — though it's still unclear how significant the changes will be. The previous generation MacBook Pro looked and felt quite bulky, so any improvement in this area would generally be welcome — provided it doesn't sacrifice thermal performance.", 'index': 14}

{'translation': 'Summary', 'index': 15}

{'translation': 'In summary, the first touchscreen MacBook Pro is shaping up to be an exciting upgrade. Since Apple raised prices in June due to a memory crisis, the new product will be priced even higher — the 14-inch model is expected to start at US$2,499, while the 16-inch model will be US$2,999.', 'index': 16}

{'translation': 'Are you excited about a touchscreen MacBook? Will you buy one immediately upon release, or wait and see for the cheaper 14-inch base model? Let us know in the comments.', 'index': 17}
